title: Clicking on the name/album art on the expanded media player widget should open the app
line: Clicking the album art or the song title in the Media Player popup now brings the player's window to the front.
explanation: The album art and the track title, artist and album in the expanded Media Player popup had no click handling, so clicking them did nothing. The only way to bring the playing app forward was the Open entry in the widget's right-click menu. The change adds a TapHandler (and a pointing-hand cursor) over the album art and details area, enabled only when the player supports Raise; a left click raises the player through MPRIS and closes the popup, like the Open action.

commits.message:
applets/mediacontroller: open the player when clicking the album art

The only way to bring the player's window forward was the Open item in
the context menu, which few people find. Now clicking the album art or
the track details in the popup raises the player and closes the popup.

BUG: 440453

media.caption: Master: clicking the album art, then the song title, does nothing; the player's window doesn't appear
With the fix: clicking the album art brings the player's window up and closes the popup
Master: popup still open after clicking the title, no player window
With the fix: clicking the song title raised the player's window

reviews.text: Minimal, idiomatic Qt 6 change adding a left-click TapHandler and pointing-hand HoverHandler gated on root.canRaise to the album art and track details area in ExpandedRepresentation.qml. It reuses root.raise(), closes the popup, preserves touch gestures and footer/context-menu interactions, and is cleanly verified on Wayland.

This does what the reporter asked: a left click on the album art or the track details raises the current player through the same root.raise() as the existing Open context action, and it only works when the player supports CanRaise. Using a TapHandler plus a HoverHandler cursor on albumRow is idiomatic. It cannot reach the footer controls, and closing the popup through root.expanded = false matches what the Notifications applet already does inside the tray. The before/after media show Raise being called and the window coming up. Minor nit: there is still no keyboard way to do the same thing, apart from the context menu, and the explanation's 'like the Open action' about closing the popup is loose wording.
